content:
According to this page in the lean reference manual, lake has some built-in capacity for running tests associated with a project. This is fairly poorly documented currently and I'd like to suggest to the lake maintainers that this be better documented, ideally with some examples of projects using tests.

That being said, I wonder if there are any blog posts or other guides written by people about what the current best practices are for Lean testing and test libraries. This spec test library seems to exist: https://reservoir.lean-lang.org/@argumentcomputer/LSpec , I'm not sure if there's anything else like it in common use. I'm also curious what people who are maintaining lake projects that require some amount of testing are doing in practice.

What we (in argumentcomputer/ix) take from lake test is simply the integration that's allowed by tagging a particular executable (registered in the lakefile) as the test driver. From there, we're on our own.

Regarding the testing lib itself, LSpec predates several Lean 4 updates and we're still rolling with it. But I'd honestly love to be able to use an official test lib coming out of the box in the Lean 4 toolchain to release the burden of maintaining our own implementation
Ah, forgot to mention, you can pass arguments to lake test by saying lake test -- foo bar baz. If your test driver implementation is ready to take arguments, that's how you provide them

Greg Shuflin said:

According to this page in the lean reference manual, lake has some built-in capacity for running tests associated with a project. This is fairly poorly documented currently and I'd like to suggest to the lake maintainers that this be better documented, ideally with some examples of projects using tests.

Now, onto Greg's actual point, I'm in agreement with that assessment. The documentation page barely shows how to actually tag a test driver. It mentions @[test_driver] only once, not in an example lakefile snippet.
and #39934 updates Mathlib CI to use lake lint, as I didn't previously understand that was possible with an upstream lint_driver.
